messages:
Nora Kim: Quick sync — proposal to tighten model catalog rows for power users. Mock: https://figma.com/file/xyz-compact-rows
Ethan Moore: Love the density, but metric meaning gets invisible. Can we keep p95 visible and collapse p50/cost into a hover card?
Priya Nair: Accessibility flag: the new teal badge (#1FBBA6) may fail contrast on 12px text in light theme. Please run WCAG and consider a darker tone or white text with outline.
Jon Chen: Keyboard flow: NAME -> METRICS -> PIN -> ACTIONS. Make pin reachable via Enter/Space; global shortcut `P` for quick-pin with a tooltip in the shortcuts modal.
Maya Ortiz: Microcopy: change pin label to "Pin version for compare" (clearer). Also add confirmation toast: "Pinned {model} {ver} — showing in compare" with an undo action.
DesignBot: Accessibility check: #1FBBA6 contrast ratio 3.8:1 on 12px; fails AA. Suggest #138F74 or add 2px stroke. Also add aria-pressed and aria-label for pin control.
Priya Nair: Screen reader note: when a row expands (shows p50/cost), announce via polite aria-live: "Details for {model} {ver} expanded". And announce pinned state changes.
Ethan Moore: Badge semantics question: product prefers p95 latency, infra wants cost. Proposal: primary badge = p95 latency; hover card = p50 + estimated cost (tokens/request, GPU-score). Keeps UX simple but informative.
Jon Chen: I'll draft a short experiment plan: control = current table, variant = compact rows + pin shortcut. Metrics: time-to-pin, keyboard activation rate, compare launches, and perceived clarity from a 15-user usability run.
Maya Ortiz: Also ensure keyboard visible focus ring for whole row; when row focused, Space toggles expansion, Enter opens details panel. Test with VoiceOver and NVDA.
Nora Kim: Thanks — action items: Priya color + ARIA, Ethan hover copy, Jon experiment spec, Maya microcopy + toasts. I'll open tickets and link prototype by EOD.
DesignBot: Created ticket UI-3788 for compact-row experiment and UI-3789 for badge color update.
Nora Kim: Great, appreciate the quick feedback!
